question: What is the primary clinical purpose of using a bedside glucometer in an emergency ward?
explanation: A bedside glucometer provides fast blood sugar readings, which is vital when assessing a patient with sudden confusion or altered consciousness. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h1)

question: A pregnant woman with gestational diabetes requires regular capillary blood testing primarily to protect which outcome?
explanation: Maintaining stable blood glucose during pregnancy prevents complications that affect both the mother and the developing baby. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h1)

question: Which substance on the test strip reacts directly with blood glucose during testing?
explanation: Test strips contain specific enzymes like glucose oxidase that trigger a chemical reaction when exposed to blood sugar. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does the digital meter convert the chemical reaction on the test strip into a readable number?

options.A: It weighs the volume of blood on the strip
options.B: It measures electrical current or color change
options.C: It counts red blood cells in the sample droplet
options.D: It detects the temperature of the blood drop

explanation: The meter reads the physical changes resulting from the enzyme reaction and translates that data into a digital blood glucose value. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h2)

question: What should the nurse check on the test strip container before starting the procedure?
explanation: Using expired test strips can compromise the chemical reagents and produce inaccurate blood glucose readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why is warming a patient's cold hand recommended before performing a capillary blood draw?

options.A: It sterilizes the skin surface naturally
options.B: It improves blood flow and prevents painful squeezing
options.C: It numbs the fingertip to eliminate all pain
options.D: It activates the enzymes in the test strip

explanation: Warming increases peripheral circulation so a natural drop of blood forms easily without harsh milking that dilutes the sample with tissue fluid. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h3)

question: Why must the nurse wipe away the very first drop of blood during capillary sampling?

options.A: It carries too many white blood cells
options.B: It contains tissue fluid that dilutes the sample
options.C: It causes the digital meter to display an error code
options.D: It is contaminated with external skin bacteria

explanation: The initial drop often contains serous fluid from the puncture that alters the glucose concentration, so the second drop is more reliable. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h4)

question: What happens if a patient's skin is still wet with alcohol when the finger is pricked?

options.A: It prevents the lancing device from puncturing the skin
options.B: It causes severe bruising around the puncture site
options.C: It can alter the chemical reaction and test results
options.D: It permanently damages the digital screen of the meter

explanation: Residual alcohol mixes with the blood sample, leading to false high or low readings due to chemical interference. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is the typical normal fasting blood glucose range for a healthy adult?
explanation: A fasting blood sugar between 70 and 99 mg/dL falls within the standard normal physiological range for non-diabetic adults. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h5)

question: How should a nurse classify a random capillary blood glucose reading of 55 mg/dL in a conscious patient?
explanation: Any blood glucose value falling below 70 mg/dL is categorized as hypoglycemia and requires prompt corrective action. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h5)

question: When is a quality control test using control solution necessary for a glucometer?

options.A: When opening a new vial of test strips
options.B: Before every single patient blood test
options.C: Once every three years during routine servicing
options.D: Only when the battery indicator light flashes red

explanation: Running control solution checks ensures that new strips and the meter are functioning correctly together. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why must test strips be stored in their original container with the lid tightly closed?

options.A: To protect the chemical reagents from environmental moisture
options.B: To keep the electronic chips inside the strips warm
options.C: To prevent the expiration date from fading away
options.D: To stop the strips from changing their physical color

explanation: Humidity damages the sensitive enzymes on test strips, leading to false or erratic glucose readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is a common cause of an unexpectedly high blood glucose reading after a patient eats?

options.A: Low room temperature affecting the meter screen
options.B: Using a lancet that is too small for the finger
options.C: Excessive pressure applied during blood collection
options.D: Food residue remaining on the patient's skin

explanation: Sugar from food or drink on unwashed fingers can falsely elevate capillary blood glucose readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h7)

question: What should the nurse do first when a glucometer displays an error code on the screen?

options.A: Record the error code as a normal patient reading
options.B: Check the battery status and clean the strip port
options.C: Discard the entire glucometer device immediately
options.D: Administer emergency insulin based on the last reading

explanation: Most error codes are caused by power issues or dirt inside the testing chamber, which are easily fixed by maintenance steps. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why should lancing devices never be shared between different patients in a hospital?

options.A: The plastic casing will melt during chemical disinfection
options.B: Shared devices automatically drain the battery faster
options.C: Blood can backflow into the internal mechanical parts
options.D: Different patients require different color lancets

explanation: Internal parts of reusable lancing devices can trap microscopic blood droplets, transmitting pathogens if used on multiple people. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h8)

question: Which infection control practice is NOT appropriate when performing bedside blood glucose testing?

options.A: Reusing a multi-patient lancing device if the needle is changed
options.B: Wearing clean non-sterile gloves during the sampling procedure
options.C: Performing hand hygiene before putting on and after removing gloves
options.D: Disposing of used lancets in a puncture-resistant sharps box

explanation: Multi-patient lancing devices pose a cross-infection risk and must be avoided in healthcare settings even with a new needle. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T5#GNS212_U4_T5_h8)
